subject: Clarification: How are day boundaries treated for SOC 2 reporting windows?
messages:
From: Pamela Gomez <pamela.gomez@ctrl-assurance.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Audit Team <ops-audit@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick question on reporting window inclusivity

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for sending the SOC 2 Type II materials. We have one quick clarification before we finalize the testing plan for Acme: when your SOC 2 report references a report period (for example, "October 1, 2025 - September 30, 2026"), how should we interpret the end-of-day inclusivity? Specifically: does Redwood treat the final day of the window as inclusive through 23:59:59 in Redwood's local time, or is the coverage defined at the UTC midnight boundary?

Also: for point-in-time evidence (e.g., "snapshot as of 2026-09-30"), do you produce a single consistent snapshot tied to a known timestamp, or do you provide per-service artifacts with their own capture timestamps? We want to avoid mismatches where different systems claim slightly different cutover moments.

If helpful, a short sentence we can include in our audit working papers about your approach would be ideal.

Best,
Pamela
Pamela Gomez
Senior Auditor, Ctrl Assurance
[Attachment: audit-request-checklist.xlsx (xlsx, 14KB)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Pamela Gomez <pamela.gomez@ctrl-assurance.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T10:04:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Quick question on reporting window inclusivity

Pamela — thanks for the clear question. Short answer up front: we define report-window end dates inclusive at the customer-configured timezone boundary for the tenant, and we also emit a coordinated point-in-time timestamp for cross-system snapshots. Longer detail below.

Details / what we provide:
- Inclusive day semantics: by default, Redwood treats a period labelled through YYYY-MM-DD as inclusive through 23:59:59.999 in the tenant's configured timezone (most customers use US/Pacific or UTC). For hosted tenants where timezone was not explicitly configured historically, we default to UTC for audit evidence consistency.
- Coordinated snapshot: for Type II evidence we create a coordinator-signed snapshot manifest (manifest includes a single ISO-8601 timestamp in UTC and a list of artifact filenames + per-artifact capture timestamps). That manifest is the authoritative point-in-time marker used by auditors to reconcile evidence.
- Per-service timestamps: individual artifacts (logs, KV cache dumps, DB export) may show capture timestamps with sub-second variance; the manifest documents those and indicates if any artifact was captured within a small roll-forward window (typical window: up to +00:05:00 for coordination).

If you need a strict cutoff at an exact UTC second instead of the tenant timezone behavior, we can produce a UTC-cut snapshot (we do this for customers who request "point-in-time at midnight UTC"). Let us know which you prefer for Acme.

Irene and Marissa — tagging you for evidence packaging and to confirm the default timezone for the Acme tenant and whether we have a manifest drafted. Karthik, can the governance team confirm the default fallback is UTC for tenants that never explicitly chose a timezone?

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Head of Security Program
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none]

From: Pamela Gomez <pamela.gomez@ctrl-assurance.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Audit Team <ops-audit@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T12:45:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Quick question on reporting window inclusivity

Thanks — that's very helpful. For Acme we'd prefer the manifest approach with an explicit UTC timestamp (their internal controls group wants a single canonical UTC point-in-time for the evidence folder). Can you confirm you can provide:

1) A manifest file that lists all artifacts included in the evidence package with a single manifest_utc_timestamp field (ISO 8601 UTC).
2) CSV of the request logs and the KV cache export used for the snapshot.
3) A short bridge letter sentence we can attach that explains your "inclusive through 23:59:59" default and notes the manifest timestamp supersedes conflicting per-artifact microvariance.

If you can provide those items as attachments (or a link to a secured drive) by 2026-11-05 we can wrap testing on our side that week.

Best,
Pamela

On Wed, Nov 3, 2026 at 10:04 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Pamela — thanks for the clear question. Short answer up front: we define report-window end dates inclusive at the customer-configured timezone boundary for the tenant, and we also emit a coordinated point-in-time timestamp for cross-system snapshots. Longer detail below.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Pamela Gomez <pamela.gomez@ctrl-assurance.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-04T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Quick question on reporting window inclusivity

Pamela — attaching the artifacts for Acme as requested. Summary of what we attached to this thread: 
- SOC2_manifest_acme_20261101.json [Attachment: SOC2_manifest_acme_20261101.json (json, 8KB)] — includes manifest_utc_timestamp: "2026-11-01T23:59:59Z" and per-artifact capture timestamps.
- kv-cache-snap-20261101.csv [Attachment: kv-cache-snap-20261101.csv (csv, 1.2MB)]
- request-logs-20261101.csv [Attachment: request-logs-20261101.csv (csv, 2.8MB)]
- Draft bridge sentence (below) and a PDF bridge letter stub for signature. [Attachment: SOC2_bridge_letter_draft_20261103.pdf (pdf, 92KB)]

Draft bridge sentence you can cite in the working papers:
"Redwood Inference defines the SOC 2 report period end date as inclusive of the calendar day through 23:59:59.999 in the tenant's configured timezone. For audit evidence, Redwood produces a coordinated manifest that records a single canonical UTC timestamp which auditors should treat as the authoritative point-in-time for reconciling per-service capture timestamps."

Notes / exceptions:
- For older archived tenants that never set a timezone we used UTC as the fallback; Acme's tenant was updated to America/Los_Angeles on 2026-04-12, but the audit manifest has been generated in UTC as requested.
- If auditors need a strict second-by-second lock (no roll-forward window), we can re-run artifact captures on a scheduled freeze; this typically requires a 24-hour coordination window to avoid customer impact.

Next steps: Pamela, I uploaded the evidence bundle to a secure drive and shared the DocuSign link for the bridge letter. Links are included above. Let me know if you want the manifest as CSV instead of JSON and we can provide both.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Manager, Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
